sealed_thresholds.note: registered BEFORE measurement; never tuned to results (Art. XXVII)
sealed_thresholds.ensemble: NONE (single-attacker calibration only; majority-vote ensembles are deferred by the R412 directive)

escalation.reason: measured FPR 1.0 > sealed bar 0.3 (Art. L: the attacker is measured non-selective; its KILL is inadmissible as a terminal verdict and is escalated with the objection preserved)
escalation.rule: the instrument's KILL is measured non-selective (FPR above the sealed bar); the objection is preserved verbatim and ESCALATED for adjudication — the candidate is NOT killed by this attack alone (Art. L); the deterministic gates are unchanged

preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism assumes that even low positive voltage can cause PID, but the evidence [doi:10.1155/2018/3286124] shows that PID primarily occurs under negative bias, not positive voltage, making the fundamental premise flawed.

The candidate fails to address temperature and humidity boundary conditions critical to PID, as established in [doi:10.3390/en12224230], which shows these factors significantly influence PID severity regardless of voltage polarity.

The evidence [doi:10.1038/s41598-025-26765-9] demonstrates that PID is primarily driven by ion migration under sustained negative bias, not voltage polarity alternation, directly contradicting the proposed intervention mechanism.

The candidate provides no evidence that periodic polarity reversal outperforms the baseline of proper module encapsulation and edge isolation techniques already proven effective in [doi:10.1038/s41598-026-49258-9].

Implementing voltage polarity reversal in existing high-voltage strings would require complete system redesign incompatible with standard PV inverters and string configurations, making retrofitting impractical.
The 25-year test prediction fails to account for the cumulative stress from repeated polarity switching cycles that may accelerate other failure modes not measured in the proposed test.
